AccessControlMode.description: How a port decides who may use it (#162).
AccessControlMode.title: AccessControlMode

AccountPrivilege.description: What a local account of a device may do (#175).
AccountPrivilege.title: AccountPrivilege

Acknowledgement.description:
A finding the user has accepted (#186): shown apart, not counted as a problem.

Matches either one finding (``finding_id``, stable across runs) or every finding of
``rule_id`` that names ``target`` among its objects. ``until``: expires then (the finding
comes back and ``ack.expired`` says so). ``fingerprint``: lapses when the finding's message
changes (:func:`finding_fingerprint`).
Acknowledgement.title: Acknowledgement

AddressSource.description: How a client got one of its addresses (#183).
AddressSource.title: AddressSource

Annotation.description:
What the user knows about one object (#186): label, purpose, owner, notes, expectations.

``target`` is a model id (:func:`target_kind`): a device id, ``<device>/port/<name>``,
``<site>/segment/<key>``, ``<device>/subnet/<name>`` or ``client/<mac>``. A network's
purpose stays in the desired state's ``segments[].purpose``; ``purpose`` here is free text.
Annotation.title: Annotation

AnnotationSource.description: Where an annotation or acknowledgement comes from.
AnnotationSource.title: AnnotationSource

Blocklist.description:
A list of blocked names a DNS service uses (Unbound DNSBL, AdGuard filter, Pi-hole list).

``name`` is the list's name or the host of its URL: never the full URL, which can carry a
subscription token.
Blocklist.title: Blocklist

CaptivePortal.description:
A captive portal (guest login page) of a device, ``object_id(device, "portal", <name>)``
(#460). Read with ``interfaces``; read-only. Never a voucher, a shared password, a RADIUS
secret or an API key: there is no field for them, also not in ``vendor_extra``.

``segments`` and ``wlans`` are what the portal covers, as far as the device says (a
MikroTik hotspot sits on an interface, an Omada portal on SSIDs, an OPNsense zone on
interfaces); both empty: not known.
CaptivePortal.title: CaptivePortal

Certificate.description:
A certificate stored on a device (VPN, RADIUS, web proxy, CA; #330),
``object_id(device, "cert", <name>)``.

The facts are those of :class:`CertificateFacts`, read from the device's list of
certificates. Adapters report only public data: the private key, its passphrase and the
certificate request never enter the model, not even in ``vendor_extra`` (the device
only says whether a key exists: ``has_private_key``). An empty ``Snapshot.certificates``
means "not read", never "none".
Certificate.title: Certificate

CertificateInfo.description:
The TLS certificate a device presents on its management port (#174).

Read by core during the pinning handshake of :class:`~signalbox.adapters.https.DeviceHttp`,
so every HTTPS integration provides it. Dates are those in the certificate: Signalbox
pins the certificate and ignores them, browsers and apps do not.
CertificateInfo.title: CertificateInfo

CertificateUse.description: What a stored certificate is used for, as far as the device says (#330).
CertificateUse.title: CertificateUse

Cipher.description: Pairwise or group data cipher of a WLAN.
Cipher.title: Cipher

ClientCategory.description: What kind of thing a client is, in the words people use.
ClientCategory.title: ClientCategory

ClientSighting.description: Where one device saw a client (#165). Same privacy class as the client itself.
ClientSighting.title: ClientSighting

ConfigState.description:
Configuration state of a device (#181). Every field is ``None`` where the device does
not say; ``False`` only where it says so (never guessed from silence).
ConfigState.title: ConfigState

CryptoProposal.description:
One algorithm combination of an IPsec proposal (#153). Names as the device gives them
in lower case (``aes256``, ``3des``, ``sha1``, ``sha256``); ``dh_group`` is the number of
the Diffie-Hellman group (2, 14, 19). None: not known.
CryptoProposal.title: CryptoProposal

DeviceAccount.description:
A local login account of a device (#175, ADR 0020): a management user, an rpcd login, a
controller administrator.

Never a password, a key or a hash of one; ``password_set`` and ``key_auth`` only say
whether there is one. Account names are often personal names: they are shown on the
device page only, never in exports, MQTT or finding messages.
DeviceAccount.title: DeviceAccount

DeviceHealth.description:
Vital signs of a device at observation time (capability ``health``).

Every value is optional: devices report very different subsets. Values change on every
observation; rules compare them with thresholds and the history, never as drift.
DeviceHealth.title: DeviceHealth

DeviceMulticast.description:
Multicast of one device (#161): snooping per bridge and the reflectors. ``[]``: read,
none.
DeviceMulticast.title: DeviceMulticast

DeviceTime.description:
Clock, time zone and NTP of a device (capability ``time``).

``clock`` is the device's time when it was read and ``read_at`` Signalbox's own time at that
moment, so :meth:`offset_seconds` is the device's clock error, give or take
``uncertainty_seconds`` (half the request's round trip).
DeviceTime.title: DeviceTime

DeviceUpnp.description:
UPnP IGD, NAT-PMP and PCP of one gateway beyond the on/off state, which is the
:class:`ManagementService` of kind ``upnp`` (#176, ADR 0029). ``None``: not reported.
DeviceUpnp.title: DeviceUpnp

DfsState.description: Radar detection state of a radio on a DFS channel (#172).
DfsState.title: DfsState

Dhcp6PrefixPool.description: A pool of prefixes a DHCPv6 server delegates to downstream routers (prefix delegation).
Dhcp6PrefixPool.title: Dhcp6PrefixPool

Dhcp6Server.description:
A DHCPv6 server on one network, ``object_id(device, "dhcp6", <name>)`` (#151); the
DHCPv4 counterpart is :class:`DhcpServer`. Read with the ``dhcp`` capability.
Dhcp6Server.title: Dhcp6Server

DhcpLease.description:
One entry of a DHCP server's lease table (#183).

Lease host names, client ids and vendor classes identify devices and people: they are client
data like :attr:`Client.hostname` (kept in the store, shown to signed-in users, neutralised
in recordings).
DhcpLease.title: DhcpLease

DhcpOption.description: A DHCP option the server hands out that has no typed field (#183).
DhcpOption.title: DhcpOption

DhcpRelay.description:
A DHCP relay on a segment (#183), ``object_id(device, "dhcp-relay", <segment key>)``.

Read with the ``dhcp`` capability: a segment with a relay needs no DHCP server of its own.
DhcpRelay.title: DhcpRelay

DnsForwarder.description:
Where a DNS service forwards lookups to: an address and a port (#241).

Accepts a bare address (port 53), ``address:port``, ``[IPv6]:port`` or dnsmasq's
``address#port``; older snapshots stored bare addresses.
DnsForwarder.title: DnsForwarder

DnsService.description:
A DNS server on a device, ``object_id(device, "dns", <name>)``.

A device may run several (#241): Unbound on another port next to AdGuard Home, dnsmasq next
to Unbound. Each has its own id and port.
DnsService.title: DnsService

DnsTransport.description: How a resolver talks to an upstream (#182).
DnsTransport.title: DnsTransport

DynamicDns.description:
A dynamic DNS client of a device (#154), ``object_id(device, "ddns", <name>)``.

Read with ``interfaces``. Never an account name, password or token: there is no field for
them, also not in ``vendor_extra``. The hostname identifies the household: shown behind a
click like an uplink's address, never exported.
DynamicDns.title: DynamicDns

DynamicPortMapping.description:
A port mapping a client opened on a gateway through UPnP IGD, NAT-PMP or PCP (#176, ADR
0029). Descriptions often carry names of apps or devices: they stay local, never in
exports for others. The device a mapping belongs to is found from ``internal_address``
through the clients of the network.
DynamicPortMapping.title: DynamicPortMapping

EvidenceSource.description: What kind of observation supports a link drawn from MAC tables (#378).
EvidenceSource.title: EvidenceSource

Expected.description:
Typed expectations about one object; each field applies to the kinds named.

Checks read them to stay silent (or be more precise) where the user has said what is
intended. None: nothing said.
Expected.title: Expected

FastTransition.description: 802.11r details of a WLAN (#168); every value None where the device does not say.
FastTransition.title: FastTransition

FdbEntry.description:
One entry of a device's forwarding database (MAC address table, #160): ``mac`` is
reachable through ``port_id``, as the device reports it, not merged into clients.

Read with ``clients`` (or ``interfaces`` where an integration has no client read); no
adapter API version needed. A controller reports the entries of the switches it manages
under their device ids. Personal data like clients: not in ``GET /api/network``, never in
MQTT.
FdbEntry.title: FdbEntry

FdbKind.description: How a MAC address got into a forwarding database (#160).
FdbKind.title: FdbKind

Firewall.description:
The packet filter and NAT of one device (#135), ``<device>/firewall``.

Read with the ``firewall`` capability (adapter API 1.4). A device without a ``Firewall``
is "not read", never "filters nothing": that is ``enabled = False``.
Firewall.title: Firewall

FirewallChain.description: Which traffic a rule sees, in netfilter terms.
FirewallChain.title: FirewallChain

FirewallMatch.description: Source or destination of a rule: every given part must match; empty parts match all.
FirewallMatch.title: FirewallMatch

FirewallRule.description:
One filter rule. The list order on :class:`Firewall` is the evaluation order: the first
rule that matches decides (adapters put OPNsense floating, group and interface rules, or
nftables jumps they can flatten, into that order).
FirewallRule.title: FirewallRule

FirewallZone.description:
A group of interfaces the rules refer to by name.

OpenWrt ``zone``, an OPNsense interface (``lan``, ``opt2``) or interface group, a MikroTik
interface list (or a single interface a rule names), an nftables ``iifname`` set, a
Fritz!Box network (LAN, guest, internet). The adapter maps the vendor's interfaces to model
objects; an interface it cannot map stays out (and ``complete`` is false).
FirewallZone.title: FirewallZone

FirmwareChannel.description: The release channel a device follows (#181).
FirmwareChannel.title: FirmwareChannel

ForeignServer.description:
A DHCP server or IPv6 router seen answering on a network (#184).

``id`` is ``<site>/foreign/<kind>/<segment key>/<server MAC or address>``. ``known_as``:
the known device it is (set by core, :func:`signalbox.foreign.known_server`); ``None``:
not a server Signalbox knows, a *foreign* one (checks ``dhcp.foreign-server``,
``ra.foreign-router``). Probe answers are stored (the latest per id, ``first_seen`` kept);
device sightings come from the snapshots.
ForeignServer.title: ForeignServer

FrameTypes.description: Which frames a port accepts on ingress (802.1Q acceptable frame types).
FrameTypes.title: FrameTypes

FtKeyHolder.description: Where an 802.11r access point keeps the pairwise master keys (#168).
FtKeyHolder.title: FtKeyHolder

GatewayGroup.description:
Uplinks that back each other up or share the load (#150),
``object_id(device, "gateway-group", <name>)``. Read with ``interfaces``.
GatewayGroup.title: GatewayGroup

GatewayGroupMember.description: One member of a gateway group (#150): a gateway or an uplink, with its tier and weight.
GatewayGroupMember.title: GatewayGroupMember

LacpRate.description: How often the far end is asked to send LACPDUs: every 30 s (slow) or every second.
LacpRate.title: LacpRate

LagHashPolicy.description: Which header fields pick the member for a frame (transmit hash policy).
LagHashPolicy.title: LagHashPolicy

LagMemberState.description:
What a member of a LAG says about itself and its LACP partner (#157). ``None``: not
reported. Partner data is there only for LACP members whose far end answers.
LagMemberState.title: LagMemberState

LagMode.description:
How a link aggregation (LAG, bond, lagg) spreads traffic and agrees with the far end
(#157, ADR 0022). Only the LACP modes negotiate: the others are static on the cable.
LagMode.title: LagMode

LinkEvidence.description: One observation behind a link of origin ``mac`` (#378): shown with inferred links.
LinkEvidence.title: LinkEvidence

LogKind.description: What a device sends to a log or monitoring target (#180).
LogKind.title: LogKind

LogTarget.description:
A remote target a device sends logs, flow records, traps or metrics to (#180, ADR 0018).

Part of :attr:`Device.log_targets`; the address is the user's own collector (internal,
not a secret). Never a credential: no SNMP trap community, no TLS key.
LogTarget.title: LogTarget

MacFilter.description:
MAC address filter of an SSID (#162). Only the mode and the number of entries are read:
the addresses of the people who use the network stay on the device.
MacFilter.title: MacFilter

MacSighting.description:
A managed device's MAC address seen on a port in an earlier round (#378): kept for
:data:`~signalbox.sightings.MAC_HOLD` so that links do not come and go as ARP and MAC
table entries age out between reads.
MacSighting.title: MacSighting

ManagementService.description:
A management service a device offers (#173), ``object_id(device, "service", <key>)``.

One object per service the device has, enabled or not: an integration that reads services
reports every one it knows, so an empty list means "not read", never "none". Read with the
``interfaces`` capability (no API version needed).

Where it listens: ``listen`` (addresses), ``interfaces`` (ports) and ``segments``
(networks) are restrictions the device itself applies; all empty means every address on
every interface. ``allowed_from`` is the service's own address filter (MikroTik
``address``), not the firewall: Signalbox cannot see firewall rules yet (#135), so
:meth:`Network.service_segments` and :meth:`Network.service_from_wan` answer from these
fields only.
ManagementService.title: ManagementService

MappingOrigin.description: How a dynamic port mapping was asked for (#176).
MappingOrigin.title: MappingOrigin

MedDeviceClass.description: LLDP-MED device class a neighbour announces (ANSI/TIA-1057, #163).
MedDeviceClass.title: MedDeviceClass

MeshLinkKind.description: How two nodes are connected wirelessly (#171).
MeshLinkKind.title: MeshLinkKind

MeshMembership.description: A device's place in a Wi-Fi mesh (#171).
MeshMembership.title: MeshMembership

MeshPeer.description:
A wireless backhaul neighbour a node reports by MAC address (#171): the other end is
not known to the node as a device. Core finds the device by the MAC address (a port, or the
BSSID of an SSID) and draws the link (:func:`signalbox.topology.mesh_peer_links`); a peer
that is no known device is not drawn. Where the node knows the other end's port, it reports
``Observation.wireless_links`` instead.
MeshPeer.title: MeshPeer

MeshPeerRole.description: Which way a wireless peer lies from the node that reports it (#171).
MeshPeerRole.title: MeshPeerRole

Monitor.description: How a gateway checks that an uplink reaches the internet (#150): it pings the targets.
Monitor.title: Monitor

MulticastSettings.description:
IGMP and MLD snooping and querier of one bridge of a device (#161, ADR 0028).

``None``: not reported. ``segment_id`` is the network the bridge carries when the device
says (a bridge with VLAN filtering has one entry per VLAN where the device reports it).
MulticastSettings.title: MulticastSettings

NatRule.description:
Source NAT: traffic leaving through ``zones`` gets the device's address (masquerade) or
``to_address``. OpenWrt zone ``masq`` is :attr:`FirewallZone.masquerade` instead.
NatRule.title: NatRule

Neighbour.description: A device seen on a port by LLDP (or a similar protocol).
Neighbour.title: Neighbour

NeighbourProtocol.description: The discovery protocol a neighbour was learned by (#163).
NeighbourProtocol.title: NeighbourProtocol

Network.description: The merged view of all sites: what rules, topology and UI work on.
Network.title: Network

PathTrace.description:
A traceroute from a device (or Signalbox's host) to an address (#253).

``id`` is ``trace/<source>/<target>``. ``reached``: the target answered; a trace that did
not get there (unanswered hops at the end, the hop limit) is partial, and checks stay quiet
about it. ``error``: the trace could not run at all (unsupported, refused, timeout); its
``fix`` and ``remedy`` as for a read error.
PathTrace.title: PathTrace

PoeMode.description: PoE standard a port delivers power with (802.3af/at/bt, or passive PoE).
PoeMode.title: PoeMode

PoeStatus.description: What a PoE port is doing right now.
PoeStatus.title: PoeStatus

PoeSupply.description: The PoE budget of a switch (#159), in watts. ``None`` fields: not reported.
PoeSupply.title: PoeSupply

Port.description:
A port of a device.

``up`` is the link state. The configuration details below (from ``description`` on) are
filled only where the device reports them, as part of the ``interfaces`` capability;
``None`` (or an empty list) means "not reported", never "off".
Port.title: Port

PortAccessControl.description:
802.1X, MAC authentication and port security of a port (#162); ``None`` fields: not
reported. Read with ``interfaces``.
PortAccessControl.title: PortAccessControl

PortCounters.description:
Traffic and error counters of a port as the device reports them (#158): monotonic
totals since ``counters_since`` (the last reset or boot), they restart at zero on a reboot.
``None``: not reported. Deltas and rates are computed by the core from two reads
(:mod:`signalbox.counters`), never by adapters.
PortCounters.title: PortCounters

PortForward.description:
Destination NAT: connections to an external port go to an internal address.

OPNsense NAT port forward, OpenWrt ``redirect`` (DNAT), MikroTik ``dstnat``, Fritz!Box port
sharing; an exposed host (DMZ) is a forward without ``external_ports``.
PortForward.title: PortForward

PortMedia.description: Physical medium of a wired port (wireless ports are ``PortKind.WIRELESS``).
PortMedia.title: PortMedia

PortPoe.description: PoE state of one port of a power sourcing switch (#159). ``None`` fields: not reported.
PortPoe.title: PortPoe

PortRange.description: A port or an inclusive range of ports.
PortRange.title: PortRange

PortRole.description:
Where a port sits in the device's internal structure (#252, ADR 0008).

``Port.kind`` says what a port is made of (Ethernet, Wi-Fi, bridge); the role says where
it sits: a jack on the case, the internal port between the CPU and a switch chip, or an
interface built on top of other ports (``Port.lower``).
PortRole.title: PortRole

PortalAuth.description: How a captive portal lets a guest in (#460), in the device's own terms.
PortalAuth.title: PortalAuth

PrefixSource.description: Where the prefix of an IPv6 subnet comes from (#151).
PrefixSource.title: PrefixSource

PurposeSource.description: Where a purpose came from. Declared beats reported beats heuristic.
PurposeSource.title: PurposeSource

RaMode.description: What a router does with router advertisements on a network, in the device's own terms.
RaMode.title: RaMode

RaPrefix.description: A prefix a router advertisement announces (prefix information option).
RaPrefix.title: RaPrefix

Radio.description:
A radio of an access point. The capability and current-state fields (#172) are None
where the device does not report them; a check needing them stays quiet then.
Radio.title: Radio

RadiusEndpoint.description: One RADIUS server an SSID uses: address (or host name) and port as configured.
RadiusEndpoint.title: RadiusEndpoint

RadiusPurpose.description: What a RADIUS server of a device is used for (#162).
RadiusPurpose.title: RadiusPurpose

RadiusRef.description: The RADIUS servers an enterprise SSID uses (#162). No secret, only whether it is set.
RadiusRef.title: RadiusRef

RadiusServer.description:
A RADIUS server a device knows or runs (#162, ADR 0030).

The shared secret is never read into the model: ``secret_set`` only says whether one is
configured. ``None`` everywhere: the device does not say.
RadiusServer.title: RadiusServer

ReadError.description: A capability that was declared but could not be read: becomes an "incomplete" finding.
ReadError.title: ReadError

Route.description:
One route of a device's routing table (#149, ADR 0024).

Read with ``interfaces``. Connected routes are not reported by most adapters: they are
derived from :class:`Subnet` (see :func:`signalbox.routing.next_hop`). A route of an IPv4
default is ``0.0.0.0/0``, of IPv6 ``::/0``. Routes of VPN peers can reveal remote sites:
treat them like addresses.
Route.title: Route

RouteOrigin.description: Where a route of a device comes from (#149).
RouteOrigin.title: RouteOrigin

RouterAdvert.description:
The router advertisements a device sends on one network, ``object_id(device, "ra",
<segment key>)`` (#151). Read with the ``dhcp`` capability.

``managed`` and ``other`` are the M and O flags as sent; where the device only has a mode
they follow from it (:func:`ra_flags`).
RouterAdvert.title: RouterAdvert

RoutingRule.description:
One policy routing rule (#149): traffic matching it is routed by another table.

Rules are evaluated by ascending ``priority``; the first match whose table has a route
decides. A device without rules uses the ``main`` table only.
RoutingRule.title: RoutingRule

SaePwe.description: How SAE derives the password element (``sae_pwe`` in hostapd).
SaePwe.title: SaePwe

SaeSettings.description: WPA3-SAE details of a WLAN (#167); every value None where the device does not say.
SaeSettings.title: SaeSettings

Segment.description:
A layer-2 network (VLAN) of a site.

``name`` is the merged display name. Precedence: the name of a gateway's view (the router
is where users name their networks), else the first name by device id. A name declared in
the desired state is not put here, so that drift can compare it with the reported ones; it
is ``declared_name`` and :attr:`shown_name` puts it first (declared > gateway > first, #511).
Segment.title: Segment

SegmentPurpose.description: What a network is for: the vocabulary users think in ("my IoT network").
SegmentPurpose.title: SegmentPurpose

SegmentRole.description: What a device is to a network (#165): how it takes part in it.
SegmentRole.title: SegmentRole

SegmentView.description: One device's view of a network (#165): what it calls it and how it takes part.
SegmentView.title: SegmentView

ServerOffer.description: What a server hands out, as far as the observation shows it (all optional).
ServerOffer.title: ServerOffer

ServerSighting.description:
A DHCP server or router a device saw answer, ``object_id(device, "server-seen", <key>)``.

Read with the ``dhcp`` capability (no API version). Known or not: core keeps every sighting
and decides which servers are foreign (:func:`signalbox.foreign.attach`).
ServerSighting.title: ServerSighting

ServiceKind.description: A way to manage (log in to, configure, query) a device (#173).
ServiceKind.title: ServiceKind

ServiceReflector.description:
A service that carries multicast discovery or streams between networks (#161): an mDNS
repeater, an SSDP or UDP broadcast relay, an IGMP proxy. Only its settings are read, never
the names of the services it carries.
ServiceReflector.title: ServiceReflector

Shaper.description:
A traffic shaper or smart queue of a device (#166), ``object_id(device, "shaper", <name>)``.

Read with ``interfaces``; read-only. ``download_kbps`` and ``upload_kbps`` are the rates the
shaper limits to, seen from the LAN (download: towards the clients); ``None``: that direction
is not limited or not known. ``uplink_id`` names the internet connection it shapes where the
device says; ``interface`` is the device's own name of what it sits on. A shaper that limits
one client or network (``addresses``, ``segment_id``) shows which household devices exist:
shown behind the device page only, never exported.
Shaper.title: Shaper

ShaperKind.description: The queueing discipline or mechanism of a shaper (#166).
ShaperKind.title: ShaperKind

Snapshot.description: Everything one adapter observed on one device at one time.
Snapshot.title: Snapshot

SnmpSettings.description:
SNMP details of a :class:`ManagementService` of kind ``snmp``.

Community strings and SNMPv3 passwords are secrets and never enter the model; only whether
a factory default is in use.
SnmpSettings.title: SnmpSettings

Source.description: Where an observed object came from.
Source.title: Source

SshHostKeyChange.description: An SSH host key that differs from the confirmed one (#526). Fingerprints are public.
SshHostKeyChange.title: SshHostKeyChange

StpBridge.description:
Spanning tree (or loop detection) of one bridge of a device (#155, ADR 0023).

A device has one per bridge (``Device.stp_bridges``): a MikroTik or Linux bridge, or the
whole switch of a managed switch (``port_id`` None). Runtime values (root, topology
changes) are what the device said at the last read. ``None``: not reported.
StpBridge.title: StpBridge

StpPort.description:
Spanning tree state and protection of one bridge port (#155, ADR 0023).
``None``: not reported.
StpPort.title: StpPort

StpProtocol.description: Loop protection of a bridge (#155, ADR 0023).
StpProtocol.title: StpProtocol

TraceHop.description: One hop of a trace: the router that answered for this TTL.
TraceHop.title: TraceHop

Tunnel.description:
A VPN interface of a device (#239), ``object_id(device, "tunnel", <interface name>)``.

Read with the ``vpn`` capability (adapter API 1.3). ``peers`` lists every peer the device
has on this interface, site-to-site and road-warrior ones alike.
Tunnel.title: Tunnel

TunnelAuth.description: How an IPsec connection authenticates (#153); never the secret itself.
TunnelAuth.title: TunnelAuth

TunnelChild.description: A child SA / phase 2 / traffic selector pair of an IPsec connection (#153).
TunnelChild.title: TunnelChild

TunnelPeer.description:
One peer of a tunnel: the other end as this device knows it (#239).

Never the pre-shared key; ``preshared_key`` only says whether one is set. The endpoint
is the other site's public address: shown behind a click like an uplink's, never exported.
TunnelPeer.title: TunnelPeer

TunnelSession.description: A client connected to an OpenVPN server (#153). No password, no key.
TunnelSession.title: TunnelSession

UnknownMulticast.description: What a bridge does with multicast frames nobody joined (#161).
UnknownMulticast.title: UnknownMulticast

Uplink.description:
A gateway's connection to its provider (WAN), ``object_id(device, "uplink", <name>)``.

Read with the ``interfaces`` capability. WAN addresses are not :class:`Subnet` objects: the
uplink is not a network of the site. The public address and the delegated IPv6 prefix
identify the household: shown in the UI behind a click, never exported (MQTT, reports).
Uplink.title: Uplink

UplinkHealth.description: What the gateway's monitor currently sees of an uplink (#150): a current value, not drift.
UplinkHealth.title: UplinkHealth

UplinkKind.description: How a gateway reaches its provider (or the router in front of it).
UplinkKind.title: UplinkKind

UplinkState.description: How an uplink or group member is doing, as the gateway's monitor says (#150).
UplinkState.title: UplinkState

UpnpAclRule.description:
One permission rule of a UPnP daemon (miniupnpd ``allow``/``deny``): which clients may
map which external ports to which internal ports (#176).
UpnpAclRule.title: UpnpAclRule

UpnpProtocol.description: Port mapping protocols a gateway answers (#176).
UpnpProtocol.title: UpnpProtocol

UpsStatus.description: A UPS monitored by the device (NUT on OPNsense, ``/system/ups`` on MikroTik).
UpsStatus.title: UpsStatus

WifiScanResult.description:
An access point a radio heard (#169, ADR 0025): a neighbour's network, or one of ours.

Data about other people's networks: kept on the server, out of ``GET /api/network``,
exporters and MQTT (:meth:`Network.without_neighbour_networks`), shown in the device's
wireless section only. No stations of foreign networks are ever stored.
WifiScanResult.title: WifiScanResult

WirelessAssociation.description:
What an access point knows of a client's Wi-Fi association (#170); None where the device
does not say. A snapshot of one moment: rules want it with history, never judge one sample.

Personal data like the client itself (presence and movement): MQTT only counts clients and
exporters never list them.

WirelessLinkInfo.description:
Radio details of a wireless backhaul link (#171). Every field is ``None`` where the
device does not say. ``radio_a``/``radio_b`` are radio ids of the two ends where known.

rule decides: OpenWrt ``forwarding`` (accept) and zone policies, OPNsense's implicit
"block in, allow out", a Fritz!Box's fixed isolation of the guest network.
